title: Full disk (ENOSPC) during a run raises raw OSError, never surfaces ERROR, and wedges the state lock

labels.name: priority:medium
labels.description: For bugs, a serious source of annoyance, but not blocking a large number of users.

body:
_This issue was created by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of @neubig._

## Summary

Suppose the persistence disk fills up (`ENOSPC`) while a conversation is running. Then `LocalConversation.run()` / `arun()` raises a raw `OSError` instead of `ConversationRunError`. The run never records its failure: there is no `ConversationErrorEvent`, the `ERROR` status is never persisted or published, and the last status clients see is `RUNNING`.

One failed deferred state flush also leaves `ConversationState._dirty` set. After that, **every** later `with state:` block raises `ENOSPC` on exit, including read-only ones. This holds until space is freed. Because of this, the agent-server's error backstop (`_mark_error_status_sync`, documented as "never raises") and its final `_publish_state_update()` also raise, and a status read through the service raises too.

The atomic writer itself is fine: the last good `base_state.json` and event files stay readable, and the conversation resumes without duplicate events once space is back. The bug is in how the run loop and the state lock handle a failed write.

## Impact

- **SDK users:** `run()` / `arun()` raises `OSError` instead of the documented `ConversationRunError`. The original error is buried under 2 more `ENOSPC` errors raised by the error handlers themselves. In memory the status is `ERROR`, but on disk it is still `running`, and no error event is recorded.
- **Agent-server clients:** subscribers get `execution_status=RUNNING` and then nothing. There is no `ConversationErrorEvent`, no `ERROR` status update, and no final state update. The UI keeps showing a running conversation that is dead. While the disk is full, reading that conversation's status through the service also raises.

## Root cause

All links are at [`af85e22`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/tree/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b).

1. **The first failure is an event write.** The agent step emits a `MessageEvent`. The persistence callback runs first in the callback chain ([local_conversation.py#L566-L578](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/impl/local_conversation.py#L566-L578)), and `EventLog.append` → `fs.write` raises `ENOSPC` ([event_store.py#L362-L364](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/event_store.py#L362-L364)). Persisting before publishing is intentional, so subscribers never hear about an event that was not saved.
2. **The run loop's error handler writes to the same full disk and has no guard** ([local_conversation.py#L2828-L2856](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/impl/local_conversation.py#L2828-L2856); async [L3375-L3404](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/impl/local_conversation.py#L3375-L3404)):
   ```python
   except Exception as e:
       with self._state:
           self._state.transition(ConversationExecutionStatus.ERROR, ...)
           ...
               self._on_event(ConversationErrorEvent(...))   # ENOSPC again
       raise ConversationRunError(...) from e                # never reached
   ```
   `_on_event` raises again. Then the `with` block's `__exit__` flushes the deferred `ERROR` save and raises a third time. That last `OSError` is what escapes `run()`.
3. **A failed flush makes the state lock fail on every exit** ([state.py#L966-L986](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/state.py#L966-L986)):
   ```python
   def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
       try:
           self._save_depth -= 1
           self._flush_deferred_save()   # raises even if exc_type is set
       finally:
           self._lock.release()

   def _flush_deferred_save(self):
       ...
       try:
           self._save_base_state(fs)
       except Exception:
           self._dirty = True            # stays dirty
           raise
   ```
   After one failed save, any `with state:` block retries the save on exit and raises, even if the block did not change anything. The flush error also replaces any exception that was already propagating out of the block.
4. **The agent-server backstop cannot surface the failure.** `_run_and_publish` sees a non-`ConversationRunError` and calls `_publish_error_event_sync` (which catches the error and logs "Failed to publish backstop ConversationErrorEvent"). It then calls `_mark_error_status_sync`. Its docstring says "Best-effort: never raises", but its `with self._conversation._state` raises on exit because of item 3 ([event_service.py#L869-L906](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/event_service.py#L869-L906), [L1809-L1830](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/event_service.py#L1809-L1830)). The `finally` then calls `_publish_state_update()`, which also uses `with state:` ([L908-L914](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/event_service.py#L908-L914)) and raises again. The `ERROR` status change cannot reach subscribers either, because its `ConversationStateUpdateEvent` goes through the same persist-first chain ("State change callback failed for field execution_status").

## Reproduction

The disk is real: a 2 MiB tmpfs that the test fills when the LLM is called, which is in the middle of a step. Only the LLM provider is stubbed (litellm completion in the SDK script; `TestLLM` in the server test).

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/ohfull && sudo mount -t tmpfs -o size=2m tmpfs /mnt/ohfull
sudo chown "$(id -u):$(id -g)" /mnt/ohfull
uv sync --dev --frozen
# SDK, sync and async
rm -rf /mnt/ohfull/*; uv run python repro_enospc.py /mnt/ohfull sync
rm -rf /mnt/ohfull/*; uv run python repro_enospc.py /mnt/ohfull async
# agent-server (save as tests/agent_server/test_enospc_repro.py)
OH_FULL_DIR=/mnt/ohfull uv run pytest tests/agent_server/test_enospc_repro.py -s -q
```

<details><summary>repro_enospc.py (SDK)</summary>

```python
"""Repro: a conversation run on a full disk (real ENOSPC from a small tmpfs).

Usage (needs a tiny tmpfs so the disk really fills up):
    sudo mkdir -p /mnt/ohfull && sudo mount -t tmpfs -o size=2m tmpfs /mnt/ohfull
    sudo chown "$USER" /mnt/ohfull
    uv run python repro_enospc.py /mnt/ohfull [sync|async]

Only the LLM provider boundary (litellm completion) is stubbed.
"""

import asyncio
import errno
import json
import os
import sys
import traceback
import uuid

from litellm.types.utils import Choices, Message as LiteLLMMessage, ModelResponse
from pydantic import SecretStr

import openhands.sdk.llm.llm as llm_mod
from openhands.sdk import LLM, Agent, Conversation
from openhands.sdk.conversation.exceptions import ConversationRunError


ROOT = sys.argv[1]
MODE = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "sync"
FILLER = os.path.join(ROOT, "filler.bin")
conv_id = uuid.uuid4()
persist = os.path.join(ROOT, "convs")


def fill_disk():
    with open(FILLER, "wb") as f:
        try:
            while True:
                f.write(b"\0" * 4096)
                f.flush()
        except OSError as e:
            assert e.errno == errno.ENOSPC


def reply(**_):
    msg = LiteLLMMessage(content="all done", role="assistant")
    return ModelResponse(
        id="r1", choices=[Choices(finish_reason="stop", index=0, message=msg)]
    )


def completion(*a, **kw):
    fill_disk()  # disk fills up while the agent is mid-step
    return reply()


async def acompletion(*a, **kw):
    fill_disk()
    return reply()


llm_mod.litellm_completion = completion
llm_mod.litellm_acompletion = acompletion


def make_conv():
    llm = LLM(model="gpt-4o", api_key=SecretStr("k"), usage_id="agent", num_retries=0)
    return Conversation(
        agent=Agent(llm=llm, tools=[]),
        workspace=ROOT,
        persistence_dir=persist,
        conversation_id=conv_id,
        visualizer=None,
    )


def persisted_status():
    d = os.path.join(persist, conv_id.hex)
    with open(os.path.join(d, "base_state.json")) as f:
        status = json.load(f)["execution_status"]
    names = os.listdir(os.path.join(d, "events"))
    return status, sum(n.startswith("event-") for n in names)


conv = make_conv()
conv.send_message("hello")
print("before run: persisted status / event files =", persisted_status())

try:
    if MODE == "sync":
        conv.run()
    else:
        asyncio.run(conv.arun())
    print("run returned normally")
except ConversationRunError as e:
    print("run raised ConversationRunError:", repr(e.__cause__))
except Exception as e:
    print(f"run raised {type(e).__name__} (not ConversationRunError): {e}")
    chain, ctx = [], e
    while ctx is not None:
        frames = traceback.extract_tb(ctx.__traceback__)
        path = " > ".join(
            f"{os.path.basename(f.filename)}:{f.lineno}({f.name})"
            for f in frames
            if "openhands/sdk/conversation" in f.filename
            or "openhands/sdk/agent" in f.filename
        )
        if path:
            chain.append(f"{type(ctx).__name__}: {path}")
        ctx = ctx.__context__
    print("  exception chain (first raised -> last raised):")
    for c in reversed(chain):
        print("   ", c)

print("in-memory status:", conv.state.execution_status.value)
print("persisted status / event files:", persisted_status())
print("ConversationErrorEvent recorded:",
      any(type(e).__name__ == "ConversationErrorEvent" for e in conv.state.events))

try:
    with conv.state:
        _ = conv.state.execution_status  # read-only use of the state lock
    print("read-only `with state:` ok")
except OSError as e:
    print("read-only `with state:` raised:", e)

# Space comes back; reopen the conversation from disk and continue.
os.remove(FILLER)
with conv.state:
    pass
print("same object after space restored: `with state:` ok; persisted =",
      persisted_status()[0])
llm_mod.litellm_completion = lambda *a, **k: reply()


async def _ar(*a, **k):
    return reply()


llm_mod.litellm_acompletion = _ar
conv2 = make_conv()
print("after reopen: status =", conv2.state.execution_status.value)
conv2.send_message("continue")
conv2.run()
print("after rerun: status =", conv2.state.execution_status.value)
print("event types:", [type(e).__name__ for e in conv2.state.events])
```
</details>

<details><summary>tests/agent_server/test_enospc_repro.py</summary>

```python
"""Repro: agent-server run when the conversations disk fills up mid-step.

Needs a tiny tmpfs at $OH_FULL_DIR (real ENOSPC), e.g.
    sudo mkdir -p /mnt/ohfull && sudo mount -t tmpfs -o size=2m tmpfs /mnt/ohfull
    sudo chown "$(id -u):$(id -g)" /mnt/ohfull
Only the LLM is scripted (TestLLM); the disk is real.
"""

import errno
import logging
import os
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from openhands.agent_server.conversation_service import ConversationService
from openhands.sdk.llm import Message, TextContent
from tests.agent_server.stress.scripts import (
    SlowTestLLM,
    start_conversation_with_test_llm,
    text_message,
)


ROOT = Path(os.environ.get("OH_FULL_DIR", "/mnt/ohfull"))
FILLER = ROOT / "filler.bin"


def fill_disk():
    with open(FILLER, "wb") as f:
        try:
            while True:
                f.write(b"\0" * 4096)
                f.flush()
        except OSError as e:
            assert e.errno == errno.ENOSPC


class DiskFillingLLM(SlowTestLLM):
    async def acompletion(self, *args, **kwargs):
        fill_disk()
        return await super().acompletion(*args, **kwargs)


@pytest.mark.timeout(60)
async def test_run_on_full_disk(caplog):
    for p in ROOT.iterdir():
        shutil.rmtree(p) if p.is_dir() else p.unlink()
    (ROOT / "ws").mkdir()
    seen = []

    class Subscriber:
        async def __call__(self, event):
            seen.append(event)

        async def close(self):
            pass

    subscriber = Subscriber()

    service = ConversationService(conversations_dir=ROOT / "persist")
    async with service:
        info = await start_conversation_with_test_llm(
            service,
            parent_llm=DiskFillingLLM.from_messages([text_message("done")]),
            workspace_dir=str(ROOT / "ws"),
            usage_id="enospc",
            initial_text=None,
        )
        es = await service.get_event_service(info.id)
        assert es is not None
        await es.subscribe_to_events(subscriber)
        seen.clear()
        caplog.set_level(logging.ERROR)

        await es.send_message(
            Message(role="user", content=[TextContent(text="hi")]), run=True
        )
        task = es._run_task
        try:
            await task
            print("\nrun task completed normally")
        except BaseException as e:
            print(f"\nrun task raised {type(e).__name__}: {e}")

        print("events/updates pushed to subscriber after send:")
        for e in seen:
            extra = getattr(e, "key", "") or getattr(e, "code", "")
            print("   ", type(e).__name__, extra, str(getattr(e, "value", ""))[:40])
        print(
            "log records:",
            [r.getMessage().splitlines()[0][:90] for r in caplog.records],
        )
        try:
            print("status via service:", await es._get_execution_status())
        except OSError as e:
            print("reading status via service raised:", e)
        FILLER.unlink()
        print("after space restored, status via service:",
              await es._get_execution_status())
```
</details>

Observed on `main` at `af85e22` (SDK, sync; async is the same with the `_arun`/`astep` frames):

```
before run: persisted status / event files = ('idle', 2)
run raised OSError (not ConversationRunError): [Errno 28] No space left on device
  exception chain (first raised -> last raised):
    OSError: local_conversation.py:2756(_run) > agent.py:857(step) > ... > response_dispatch.py:351(_emit_message_event) > ... > local_conversation.py:533(_default_callback) > state.py:496(append_event) > event_store.py:364(append)
    OSError: local_conversation.py:2841(_run) > ... > local_conversation.py:533(_default_callback) > state.py:496(append_event) > event_store.py:364(append)
    OSError: local_conversation.py:2668(run) > local_conversation.py:2829(_run) > state.py:970(__exit__) > state.py:983(_flush_deferred_save) > state.py:618(_save_base_state)
in-memory status: error
persisted status / event files: ('running', 2)
ConversationErrorEvent recorded: False
read-only `with state:` raised: [Errno 28] No space left on device
same object after space restored: `with state:` ok; persisted = error
after reopen: status = error
after rerun: status = finished
event types: ['SystemPromptEvent', 'MessageEvent', 'MessageEvent', 'MessageEvent']
```

Agent server:

```
run task raised OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device
events/updates pushed to subscriber after send:
    SystemPromptEvent
    MessageEvent
    ConversationStateUpdateEvent last_user_message_id ...
    ConversationStateUpdateEvent execution_status ConversationExecutionStatus.RUNNING
log records: [..., 'State change callback failed for field execution_status', 'Error during conversation run', 'Failed to publish backstop ConversationErrorEvent']
reading status via service raised: [Errno 28] No space left on device
after space restored, status via service: ConversationExecutionStatus.ERROR
```

## Expected behavior

- `run()` / `arun()` raise `ConversationRunError` whose cause is the original storage error, ideally as a typed persistence error so callers can tell "disk full" apart from an agent or LLM failure.
- The in-memory status becomes `ERROR`, and agent-server subscribers are told about it even though it cannot be written to disk. This should be an explicitly non-persisted notification, not a claim that the event was saved.
- A failed save does not make later read-only `with state:` blocks raise. It also does not replace an exception that is already propagating.
- Current guarantees stay: the last good snapshot stays readable, nothing that was not saved is announced as saved, and once space returns the conversation can continue without duplicate events. The repro shows these hold today.

## Suggested fix

1. In `ConversationState.__exit__`, do not let `_flush_deferred_save()` replace an in-flight exception. Log it and keep `_dirty` set so the next writer retries. Read-only blocks should not raise a stale save error. One option: re-raise the flush error only when the current block marked the state dirty.
2. In the `run()`/`arun()` `except` handlers, record the error on a best-effort basis: set the status in memory and try to emit the `ConversationErrorEvent`. Catch `OSError` around that recording and always raise `ConversationRunError(...) from e`. Consider wrapping `ENOSPC`/`EDQUOT`/`EROFS` in a typed `ConversationPersistenceError`.
3. In `EventService`, make `_mark_error_status_sync` really best-effort, as its docstring says. If the final `ConversationStateUpdateEvent`/`ConversationErrorEvent` cannot be persisted, publish it straight to subscribers, so clients do not stay on `RUNNING`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With `ENOSPC` injected during a step (a real full filesystem or a failing `FileStore.write`), sync and async `run()` raise `ConversationRunError`, and `__cause__` is the original storage error.
- [ ] After that failure, `with state:` without changes does not raise, and `_mark_error_status_sync()` does not raise.
- [ ] Agent-server subscribers receive an `ERROR` status (and an error detail) for that run, even though it was not persisted.
- [ ] The previous `base_state.json` and event files stay readable. After space is restored, a reopened conversation runs another turn, and no event is duplicated.
- [ ] A flush failure inside a `with state:` block that is already raising does not replace the original exception.

## OpenHands AI triage
**The following comments and acceptance criteria were added by the OpenHands AI agent.**

### Triage
Verified against `main` at `af85e22`. The reported failure chain is accurate: `ConversationState.__exit__` (`state.py:966-986`) calls `_flush_deferred_save()` outside any suppression, so a failed save re-raises and stays `_dirty`, wedging every later `with state:` block; the `run()`/`arun()` `except` handlers (`local_conversation.py:2828-2856`, async `3375-3404`) call `self._on_event(ConversationErrorEvent(...))` inside the same `with self._state:` block, so persist-first emission re-raises `ENOSPC` before `ConversationRunError` is raised; `EventService._mark_error_status_sync` (`event_service.py:869-886`) enters `with self._conversation._state` despite its "never raises" docstring, and the `ERROR` status update's `ConversationStateUpdateEvent` goes through the same persist-first callback (`_state_change_callback` → `conversation._on_event`, `event_service.py:1285-1302`), matching the "State change callback failed for field execution_status" log line. The reproduction drives the real run loop and agent-server run path with a real full filesystem (only the LLM boundary is stubbed), so this is a reproduced failure in the actual product workflow.

**Bounded scope:** (1) `ConversationState` deferred-save exit behavior — a flush failure must not replace an in-flight exception and must not make read-only `with state:` blocks raise; (2) the `run()`/`arun()` `except` handlers — record status and the error event on a best-effort basis and always raise `ConversationRunError` chained from the original storage error; (3) `EventService` backstops — `_mark_error_status_sync` must honor its best-effort contract, and the final `ERROR` state/error notification must reach subscribers when it cannot be persisted, without being written to the event log or claimed as saved.

**Priority: medium.** The failure is reproduced through the real run/service workflow with severe impact when it strikes (raw `OSError`, no `ERROR` surfaced, subscribers left on `RUNNING`, status reads raise, conversation wedged until space returns), and it sits in a lifecycle path the team is actively hardening (#7080, #7081). Not high: no user/customer report thread yet and the trigger is a disk-full condition rather than routine operation.

**Non-goals:**
- No new public exception type (e.g. a typed `ConversationPersistenceError`). Callers get `ConversationRunError` with the original storage error as `__cause__`; a typed storage error would be a separate additive change if maintainers want one.
- No change to the success-path persist-before-publish ordering: nothing is announced to subscribers unless it was saved. The only exception is the explicit best-effort `ERROR` notification for a run that cannot persist, which must not be written to the event log or claimed as persisted.
- No space reclamation, retry, backoff, or disk-monitoring logic; no UI or `clients/typescript/` changes (existing `ConversationStateUpdateEvent`/`ConversationErrorEvent` payloads already carry status and error detail).
- No changes to `RemoteConversation`; the defect is in local persistence failure handling.
- No change to the on-disk schema, persisted settings shape, or event payloads (no migration needed).

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] When a storage write fails mid-step (a real full filesystem or a failing write through the persistence chokepoint `FileStore.write`), both sync `run()` and async `arun()` raise `ConversationRunError` whose `__cause__` is the original storage error, not the secondary flush `OSError`.
- [ ] After that failed run, a read-only `with state:` block (no field changes) completes without raising while the disk is still full, and `EventService._mark_error_status_sync()` returns without raising (its best-effort docstring holds).
- [ ] A deferred-save failure inside a `with state:` block that is already propagating an exception does not replace the original exception; the original exception is what the caller observes (the flush error may be logged).
- [ ] The failed run records `ConversationExecutionStatus.ERROR` in memory and a `ConversationErrorEvent` on a best-effort basis; when recording itself fails because the disk is still full, `run()`/`arun()` still raise `ConversationRunError` chained from the original error.
- [ ] While the disk is full, reading the conversation's execution status through the agent-server service returns the in-memory `ERROR` rather than raising, and subscribers receive the `ERROR` status plus an error detail for that run as an explicitly non-persisted notification (not written to the event log, not claimed as saved).
- [ ] The last good `base_state.json` and event files remain readable and unchanged at their last successful save; after space is restored, the conversation can be reopened and run another turn with no duplicated events.
- [ ] Success-path persist-before-publish ordering is unchanged: a subscriber is never notified of an event or state change that was not saved.
- [ ] Validation pairs an automated CI test that injects the write failure with the repository's live-evidence requirement for persisted-state fixes: the real filesystem (tmpfs `ENOSPC`) reproduction from this issue is re-run on the fix branch and its output shows `ConversationRunError` raised, `ERROR` surfaced to subscribers, and resume without duplicates after space is restored.
